brief:
Landing page for MyAstroLuck Kundli Matching, a free Vedic horoscope matching tool for couples and families in India.

What the page must cover:
- Header: MyAstroLuck wordmark, nav links (Kundli, Matching, Panchang, Horoscope), a "Match now" button.
- Hero: headline about checking compatibility the Vedic way, one-line explanation of Ashtakoota (36 gunas), and a matching form preview with two columns (boy and girl: name, date of birth, time of birth, place of birth) and a "Check compatibility" button. Note that results are calculated with the sidereal zodiac and Lahiri ayanamsha.
- The 8 kootas explained: Varna (1), Vashya (2), Tara (3), Yoni (4), Graha Maitri (5), Gana (6), Bhakoot (7), Nadi (8), each with its points and one plain sentence on what it checks. Show the total of 36.
- How to read the score: bands 0-17 (not recommended without remedies), 18-24 (average, acceptable), 25-32 (very good), 33-36 (excellent), plus a short note that Manglik dosha and Nadi dosha are checked separately.
- FAQ: 4 questions (is it free, what if I do not know birth time, is guna milan enough on its own, what is Nadi dosha) with short honest answers.
- Footer: links, a line that MyAstroLuck gives guidance and not guarantees, copyright 2026.

Brand (use exactly): page background #faf7ef, surface #f4ecda, cards #ffffff, ink #1f1d1a, muted text #5a5045, rules #e3dacb, accent (terracotta) #a84219, accent text on accent #f8f1e3, pale accent tint #f3dcc9, dark band #28234c with text #f8f1e3. Radius 14px. Body font "Inter", heading font "Fraunces". Tone: warm, calm, precise, no hype. No testimonials, no ratings, no user counts.

MyAstroLuck provides Kundli matching and Vedic astrological analysis as an interpretive tool for self-reflection and personal insight. Astrology is an ancient analytical framework based on planetary positions; it does not constitute binding psychological, medical, legal, or financial advice.

We do not guarantee specific life, relationship, or compatibility outcomes. Human agency, mutual effort, and conscious choices remain the primary determinants of any relationship's success.

Traditional Vedic Astrology

Analyze Compatibility Through the Ashtakoota System

The traditional Vedic Kundli matching system evaluates compatibility across eight distinct dimensions, known as the Ashtakoota. By assessing 36 critical points (Gunas), it provides an objective, time-tested analysis of mental, emotional, and physical alignment between partners.

Technical Specification

All calculations are performed utilizing high-precision planetary algorithms based on the sidereal zodiac and the Lahiri ayanamsha (Chitra Paksha) to ensure accurate Nakshatra and Pada determinations.

Enter Birth Details

Partner 1 (Boy)

Partner 2 (Girl)

Your privacy is respected. Birth details are processed solely for generating compatibility calculations and are not stored permanently.

Interpreting Your Compatibility Score

The Ashtakoota system evaluates compatibility out of a maximum of 36 points (Gunas). Understanding the mathematical thresholds helps put your compatibility report into traditional perspective.

Under Threshold

0 – 17 Points

Generally not recommended for marriage under traditional Vedic standards. Indicates significant friction in core temperament, mental alignment, or health parameters.

Guidance: Requires detailed chart review and specific remedies (Upayas) if proceeding.
Acceptable

18 – 24 Points

The baseline for a stable union. Indicates average, workable compatibility where mutual understanding, effort, and mature communication can successfully bridge natural differences.

Guidance: Recommended for alliance, provided major individual doshas are absent.
Very Good

25 – 32 Points

Strong emotional, mental, and physical compatibility. Indicates high harmony, shared values, and a natural supportive alignment that fosters long-term mutual growth.

Guidance: Highly recommended. Predicts a naturally cooperative and harmonious relationship.
Excellent

33 – 36 Points

An exceptional and rare alignment of core energies. Represents profound soul-level compatibility and near-perfect synchronization across almost all analytical parameters.

Guidance: Outstanding compatibility. Rare configuration indicating seamless life path alignment.

Critical Analytical Note: Dosha Exclusions

While the numerical Guna score is a vital baseline, it represents only one facet of Vedic matching. Critical factors like Manglik Dosha (Mars afflictions) and Nadi Dosha (physiological/genetic incompatibility) are evaluated independently. A severe, uncompensated Nadi Dosha or an unmatched Manglik configuration can override a high Guna score. Comprehensive matching always cross-references the numerical score with these primary planetary placements.

Vedic Methodology

The Eight Kootas of Ashtakoota

Ashtakoota matching is a traditional, structured framework that analyzes compatibility across eight distinct dimensions. Each parameter carries a progressive weight, totaling 36 points.

The 36-Point Scale

The sum of all eight Kootas represents the total compatibility score of 36 Gunas. In Vedic tradition, a score of 18 or above indicates a balanced foundation for a harmonious partnership.

Maximum Score 36 Gunas
Minimum for Alignment 18 Gunas
Analytical Basis Lunar Constellations

Note: While a higher score indicates greater structural alignment, traditional astrologers also analyze individual planetary placements to provide a complete evaluation.

Koota 1 Max: 1 Point

Varna

Assesses work compatibility, spiritual temperament, and the natural skills and capacities of both partners.

Koota 2 Max: 2 Points

Vashya

Examines mutual dominance, emotional influence, and the power dynamic between partners to ensure balanced attraction.

Koota 3 Max: 3 Points

Tara

Analyzes birth star compatibility to indicate longevity, health, and mutual well-being throughout the partnership.

Koota 4 Max: 4 Points

Yoni

Evaluates physical compatibility, intimate bonding, and biological harmony based on animal archetypes associated with birth stars.

Koota 5 Max: 5 Points

Graha Maitri

Measures mental compatibility, intellectual friendship, and the natural alignment of the planetary rulers of both moon signs.

Koota 6 Max: 6 Points

Gana

Determines temperament compatibility, classifying individuals into Deva (divine), Manushya (human), or Rakshasa (demon) groups.

Koota 7 Max: 7 Points

Bhakoot

Analyzes emotional resonance, family welfare, and prosperity based on the relative position of the partners' zodiac signs.

Koota 8 Max: 8 Points

Nadi

Evaluates genetic compatibility, physiological balance, and the health of future offspring, carrying the highest weight in compatibility.

Clarity & Tradition

Frequently Asked Questions

Vedic compatibility is an intricate science. Here are honest, precise answers to the most common inquiries regarding Kundli Matching and Guna Milan.

Is this service completely free?

Yes. Our online Kundli Matching and Guna Milan tool is fully accessible without any hidden charges, subscriptions, or premium paywalls. We believe that foundational Vedic calculations should be freely available to anyone seeking clarity and alignment in their personal life choices.

What if I do not know my exact birth time?

An exact birth time ensures the most precise calculations for the Ascendant (Lagna) and the subtle divisional charts. If you do not know the exact minute, you can input a close estimate. However, even small discrepancies can shift the Moon's nakshatra quarters or modify the Navamsha chart. If high accuracy is desired, we recommend consulting a professional astrologer for a birth time rectification process.

Is guna milan sufficient on its own for marriage?

No. While Guna Milan (Ashta Koota) is a highly structured and reliable initial screening system based on the Moon's positions, it represents only one dimension of compatibility. A complete Vedic matching process also evaluates the strength of the Seventh House (marriage), the current planetary periods (Dashas), individual longevity, and the presence of severe planetary afflictions like Manglik Dosha.

What is Nadi dosha and why does it matter?

Nadi represents the physiological and psychological constitution (classified into Adi, Madhya, and Antya, similar to the Ayurvedic humors of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha). A Nadi Dosha occurs when both partners share the same Nadi classification. In Vedic astrology, this is assigned the highest weight of 8 points because it traditionally indicates potential challenges in progeny, genetic compatibility, and long-term health harmony.
